subject: MeridianPay pilot — spend rebound plan & batching playbook
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex@meridianpay.com>, Samira Patel <samira@meridianpay.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jul 2028 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: MeridianPay discovery — summary, spend-rebound plan & next asks

Alex / Samira,

Thanks again for the call today — good conversation. Below is a concise recap of the pain you described, the goals we heard, the levers that will materially change token economics, and proposed next steps. I attached a draft pilot estimate (redwood_meridian_pilot_estimate.xlsx) and the usage snapshot you shared.

Quick recap of what you shared (pain points)
- Token burn spikes on payment-authorizations and fraud-check flows during peak checkout (30% of daily tokens but 60-70% of cost).
- 99th-pctl latency SLOs are strict for auth paths (~120ms target).
- Budget pressure: current LLM spend exceeds runway for the three-month pilot window; finance needs clear cost reduction paths to approve commit.

Goals we agreed on
1) Demonstrate ~40–60% reduction in tokens billed for authorization/fraud flows without increasing 99th-pctl latency beyond your target.
2) Deliver a pilot with predictable monthly spend (within ±10%) so treasury can approve a short-term commit.
3) Validate output quality for decisioning models (no material regression vs current model).

Levers we propose / what we can run in the pilot
- Response-level batching for synchronous auth requests (small batches, continuous batching) — expected 10–25% token reduction for short prompts.
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated system prompts and common user context in checkout flows — expected 20–35% token reduction.
- Aggressive prompt engineering: strip boilerplate, reuse system tokens, and structured outputs to reduce generation tokens — expected 5–15% reduction.
- Model variant + quantization: moving to a quantized candidate for non-critical flows yields cost delta with minimal quality drop; fallback to full model for high-risk requests.

High-level ROI snapshot (see attached for numbers)
- Baseline: ~1.2B tokens/month across auth+fraud.
- Conservative pilot target: 45% aggregate token reduction => ~660M tokens saved/month equivalence (modeled).
- Estimated cost delta: see attached sheet (we used your histogram + our per-token rate assumptions).

Asks / next steps
1) Can you confirm finance's target monthly spend range for pilot approval? (range or max).
2) Please confirm whether we should include a private deployment option in the pilot (VPC) or if hosted API is acceptable to start. This affects infra and unit economics.
3) We propose a 6-week technical pilot (two-week config + two-week live run + two-week readout). Is that timeline workable?
4) If you want, I can schedule a short technical pre-kick next week with Rishi (engineering) to align telemetry and tracing requirements.

I'll wait for items (1) and (2) before finalizing the estimate.

Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.com] | +1 415-555-0124
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_meridian_pilot_estimate.xlsx (pilot cost model), meridian_current_usage_snapshot.csv (your histogram)
From: Alex Chen <alex@meridianpay.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Samira Patel <samira@meridianpay.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jul 2028 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MeridianPay discovery — summary, spend-rebound plan & next asks

Jordan — thanks for the thorough recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Finance target: we need to bring the pilot spend down to <= $30k/month (from current ~$95k run rate) to get quick approval. If your pilot shows predictable ~50% reduction but still ends near $50k, we'll have to justify the delta.

2) Latency: 99th-pctl must stay <= 120ms on auth. We're okay trying hosted API first if you can guarantee a regional deployment in us-west.

3) Private deployment: optional for the pilot — not required initially. We will revisit if the pilot needs private connectivity for logs.

4) On the ROI numbers: can you call out the assumptions around request batching (batch size distribution) and the expected change in 99th pctl when batching is active? We need to understand risk to latency SLO.

Also, I've attached the last 30 days of event counts in case that helps.

—Alex
Head of Platform Engineering | MeridianPay

Alex — quick follow to answer the two items you flagged (batching assumptions & latency impact).

Batching assumptions / expected behavior
- Distribution: most auth requests are sub-500 tokens; we expect median batch size of 4–8 during peak; outside peak, continuous batching will produce batch sizes of 1–3.
- Token saving per auth call: ~12–22% from response-level batching alone (conservative).
- KV/prefix cache: another ~18–30% on flows where user/context repeats within sessions.

Latency impact (99th-pctl)
- Our continuous batching runtime targets sub-5ms queueing overhead for batch assembly at this load profile when deployed in us-west (we deploy colocated serving pools).
- Worst-case added tail from batching is dominated by head-of-line waiting in artificial tests; with the small batch sizes above we model <10ms additional p99 when properly tuned.
- We will instrument and provide p50/p90/p99 dashboards in the pilot; plan includes an SLI/SLO annex.

We will keep the hosted option as default and only surface private deployment if you need firewall/VPC access for logs.

I've copied Rishi to coordinate the technical pre-kick. Rishi — can you propose 2 x 30-min slots tomorrow for a telemetry/trace alignment call?

Jordan

Date: Tue, 23 Jul 2028 10:41:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing options for MeridianPay pilot (commit / runway choices)

Alex / Jordan / team,

Following Jordan's ask on finance targets, I ran two quick scenarios in the attached estimate sheet:

1) Hosted pilot, no commit (metered) — expected month-1 spend: ~$65k (with conservative 40% token reduction). Not enough for finance target.

2) Hosted pilot with a small reserve commit (3-month minimum, capped) — we can offer a 35% effective unit discount on tokens for committed volume which gets projected month spend to ~$28–32k depending on realized reduction. This matches your <=$30k target if the pilot achieves ~45% reduction.

3) Private pilot (VPC) — added infra uplift (~+$6k/mo) but we can bake that into the commit and extend the same unit discount; in cases where log-exporting and on-prem telemetry are required this is the path.

If you can confirm which runway finance would accept (metered vs capped commit), I can convert the estimate to an explicit invoice-ready quote and include a short contract term (pilot addendum) for legal to fast-track.

Optional next step: Jordan / I can put a one-page summary for finance that shows the conservative and upside spend scenarios (two rows: meter vs commit) and the decision date you'd like to target.

Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
